item.title: Local farmer on week of protesting within Bord Bia HQ
item.description: IFA members are continuing protesting at Bord Bia in Dublin today. They are demonstrating both inside and outside the building in anger over the Chair of the company Larry Murrin importing some Brazilian beef. 6 members of the Irish Farmers Association have held a sit-down protest inside Bord Bia since last Tuesday. item.title: Cavan councillor wants clarification for landlords and tenants
item.description: A Cavan County Councillor is calling for clarification for both tenants and landlords. This is in relation to the proposed reform of the landlord tenants regulations, and the concerns that both sides have. Carmel Brady raised the issue at the most recent meeting of Cavan County Council. Advertisement It comes as the Residential Tenancies Bill 2026 sees an introduction of a minimum tenancy term of six years. item.title: Carthy calls for gov to support CoCo's law amendment
item.description: A local TD has called for the government to strengthen laws that would demonstrate a commitment to zero tolerance for violence against women and children. Local TD Matt Carthy believes that current laws are not being enforced. CoCo’s law was passed in 2020, and means that the distribution or sharing of images of another person, without their consent, is a criminal offense. item.description: Seamus Reilly 63 Bun Road, Newtownbutler, Co. Fermanagh. Seamus Reilly passed away on Monday, 9th February 2026. Peacefully at home, surrounded by his loving family. item.title: Cavan man named editor of Irish Farmers Journal
item.description: The Irish Farmers Journal has announced the appointment of Adam Woods as the new Editor of the publication. A native of Ballyconnell in Co Cavan, Adam has been an ever-present member of the Irish Farmers Journal’s senior editorial leadership team for the past decade, and has served as Deputy Editor of the publication for the past two years. item.title: Monaghan principal outlines importance of online safety
item.description: A local principal has highlighted the importance of online safety on Internet Safety Day. Mr James Sherry of Secondary School in Monaghan Town said it's "unfortunate" that students now spend such a considerable amount of time on mobile devices. As a result of this, he said it's vitally important that the whole school community of St Louis are fully aware of the dangers of the internet and social media. item.title: Mobile health unit coming to Monaghan Town
item.description: A mobile unit to raise awareness for cancers effecting men and women will be in Co. Monaghan tomorrow. Monaghan women's assembly have arranged for the Marie Keating foundation's mobile unit to come to Monaghan Town tomorrow from 11am until 11.30pm. The unit is free of charge, and will be open for both men and women outside of the courthouse in the town. item.title: Local councillor on banning mobile phones
item.description: A local councillor says banning mobile phones in all primary schools would be a step in the right direction. Cllr Aine Smith says she would like to see an outright ban on under 16s using social media. The local councillor who is also a teacher says phone pouches to date in schools have played a huge role. item.title: Garda warning about level of local scams
item.description: A Co Monaghan member of An Garda Síochána is reminding the public about the level of scams that are in operation. Sgt Stephen McCabe from Clones Garda Station says it's not just on your computer or your phone that dangers exist. He says cold calling to people's homes is something that people need to be aware of. item.title: Monaghan children with special needs 'left in limbo'
item.description: "Monaghan's children with special needs continue to be failed by the Department of Education time and time again." That's according to Paddy McAloon who is part of the 'Special Needs Active Parents' campaign. Children with special needs in Co Monaghan are trying to get into post primary schools, however only seven places are available.
